acm.images: Do not present AI-generated images as empirical evidence unless the model is the object being evaluated.
acm.name: ACM
acm.note: Reading of the official page by a research pass. An earlier secondary source summarized that ACM no longer requires disclosure of writing assistance; check the official text.

apa-journals.images: Full disclosure and verification of reproduction rights.
apa-journals.name: APA Journals

cope.images: Disclose the tool and the part of the manuscript, images or data analysis where it was used.
cope.name: COPE

elsevier.images: Creating, altering or manipulating images, figures or illustrations with generative AI is prohibited unless it is part of the method, described reproducibly in the methods.
elsevier.name: Elsevier
elsevier.note: Journal policy page; the previous URL is the policy for books. A research pass also reported exemptions for basic reference-manager functions without generative AI and for accessibility assistive technology; only the grammar, spelling and punctuation exemption was confirmed independently.

icmje.images: Describe in the methods the use of AI to collect data, analyze or create figures, stating the tool, version and manufacturer.
icmje.name: ICMJE

ieee.images: Disclose the use and verify that it does not infringe third-party rights.
ieee.name: IEEE
ieee.note: Editing and grammar enhancement is outside the policy's intent, but IEEE recommends disclosing it in the Acknowledgment section.

mdpi.images: Creating or altering figures with AI is prohibited unless the method is the object of the research.
mdpi.name: MDPI

plos.images: Allowed for illustration or summary, never for primary data, with a disclosure in the legend.
plos.name: PLOS
plos.note: Language improvements need no disclosure; disclosing AI-assisted translation is recommended. AI-generated figures are allowed for illustration or summary, with a disclosure in the figure legend.

sage.images: Do not present AI-generated images as original research; only as illustration with a disclosure.
sage.name: SAGE

springer-nature.images: Red category: AI may not be used to replace scientific judgment or to fabricate or manipulate data or images, unless it is the object of study.
springer-nature.name: Springer Nature
springer-nature.note: The author guidance classifies even low-risk uses such as language editing as requiring a description of the use and confirmation of author accountability. The previous URL is guidance for editors. The author page shows no date; policy_date comes from an earlier reading.

taylor-francis.images: Do not generate or alter figures or primary data unless they are the object of the methodology.
taylor-francis.name: Taylor & Francis

wiley.images: Do not present AI-generated images as original research images; illustrative use requires the editor's permission and a disclosure.
wiley.name: Wiley

business-management/accounting-finance.note: The 2 Anglophone journals use Chicago author-date; the Spanish-language journal uses APA. Changed from the provisional default (apa-7).

business-management/management.note: Academy of Management uses its own guide derived from APA.

health/nursing.note: Sample of 4 journals: 3 Vancouver and 1 APA (one Wiley journal was blocked). The two Spanish-language journals are split between APA and Vancouver.

health/public-health.note: 4 of 5 journals use numeric styles (Vancouver or AMA).

humanities/linguistics.note: The journal Language uses the LSA Unified Style Sheet (official source confirmed, 2007 version).

humanities/philosophy.note: The 2 Anglophone journals use their own author-date styles, grouped here as harvard; the Spanish-language journal uses APA. Changed from the provisional default (chicago-18).

life-sciences/agronomy-veterinary.note: 2 Vancouver and 1 CSE in the sample. Changed from the provisional default (apa-7).

life-sciences/biology.note: 2 of 3 journals use Vancouver; the ecology and evolution journals use CSE name-year. Changed from the provisional default (cse).

life-sciences/biotechnology.note: Nature Biotechnology uses its own numeric style, grouped here with Vancouver.

social-sciences/law.note: In Colombia a hybrid practice predominates; see rule R-22.

social-sciences/psychology.note: BMC Psychology uses a biomedical numeric template.

social-sciences/sociology.note: ASA, Chicago and APA each appear once. ASA is the field's own standard (see the open item about its edition).

stem/chemistry.note: RSC uses its own numeric style, which has no folder in the repository.

stem/computer-science.note: IEEE and ACM are tied in the sample; an Ibero-American engineering journal uses APA.

stem/physics-astronomy.note: AIP Publishing accepts three reference formats depending on the journal (numeric, alphabetical and combined). IOP Publishing splits its journals between Harvard and Vancouver (its support page blocked automated reading).

invariants.text: reporting_guideline must belong to study_designs[study_design].reporting, or to protocol_reporting when document_type is one of protocol_document_types and protocol_reporting is not empty; otherwise deny
every referenced id must exist in the manifest, except those listed in gap
defaults_by_discipline covers each leaf exactly once
default belongs to allowed when it is not null; variant belongs to the standard's variants
no two rules have the same when and incompatible effects (deny vs require)
every publisher_profile in the policy-registry exists in the manifest
each reporting guideline appears in at least one study_design

precedence.notes: Linear general order with per-attribute overrides; a journal or institution requirement wins over the discipline's default value.

care.note: No derivative works and no commercial purposes, or link to care-statement.org.

cheers-2022.license_claimed: CC BY 4.0 in The BMJ; the co-publication in Value in Health is licensed by Elsevier/ISPOR

coreq.license_claimed: Copyright 2007 ISQua and Oxford University Press

process-2023.license_claimed: CC BY 4.0 or CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 depending on the edition in International Journal of Surgery
process-2023.note: The research pass reported a later update (PROCESS 2025); verify the exact license of the issue.

sanra.note: Assessment scale, not a formal reporting guideline.

squire-2.note: Non-commercial uses only. Corrects the earlier claim that it was CC BY 4.0.

srqr.license_claimed: Copyright 2014 Association of American Medical Colleges

strobe.license_claimed: CC BY (PLOS Medicine edition); the co-publications carry publisher copyright
strobe.note: Only the PLOS Medicine or strobe-statement.org version.

trend.license_claimed: Checklist hosted by the CDC, US federal public domain, with attribution

rules.reason: Trial protocols are reported with SPIRIT 2025.
Systematic reviews follow PRISMA 2020.
Use the PRISMA-ScR extension; verify that it is current.
Meta-analyses with PRISMA 2020; add MOOSE if the studies are observational.
Case reports with CARE.
COREQ only for interviews and focus groups; SRQR is general.
SANRA is a quality scale for narrative reviews, not a formal reporting guideline.
PROCESS is specific to surgery; in other areas descriptive STROBE is adapted.
APA JARS covers quantitative, qualitative and mixed-methods research in the social sciences.
All reviewed policies ask authors to describe in the methods the use of AI to conduct the research.
All reviewed policies require disclosure of generative use; the location and wording depend on the organization.

Varies by organization: ICMJE, COPE and most publishers ask for disclosure. ACM, Springer Nature, Elsevier and SAGE exempt basic spelling and grammar correction, and Springer Nature and SAGE also exempt assistive use.
No reviewed organization accepts an AI tool as an author.
Many journals require it.
Statement of ethics approval and consent.
Institutions usually impose their own standard for theses.
The humanities convention is notes or author-date.
Footnotes do not fit short formats.
Colombian standard designed for Spanish.
Brazilian standard designed for Portuguese.

APA 7 is the most frequent norm in Colombian thesis guides sampled by two research passes, but several universities set the norm per faculty and some require ICONTEC (NTC 1486); check the institution's own guide.
There is no official legal citation standard; a hybrid practice based on an editorial manual and university guides is documented.
Reporting guidelines do not apply to these formats.

abnt-brasil.edition: NBR 6023:2025 (3rd ed., 22-Sep-2025; corrected version 2026); NBR 10520:2023 (2nd ed., 19-Jul-2023); NBR 14724:2024 (4th ed., 11-Dec-2024; in force since 11-Jan-2025)
abnt-brasil.notes: Confirmed by three independent university sources; the official ABNT catalog (paid) was not opened.

acm.notes: Numeric, with an author-year variant depending on the conference.

acs.edition: ACS Guide to Scholarly Communication (continuous digital edition; in 2020 it replaced the ACS Style Guide, 3rd ed., 2006)
acs.notes: Three citation systems: superscript number, italic number in parentheses, and author-year.

aip.notes: Accepts three reference formats: numeric, alphabetical (author-year with title) and combined. The AIP Style Manual (4th ed., 1990) is no longer the reference.

ama-11.notes: Numeric with superscripts; a system related to Vancouver with formatting differences.

apa-7.notes: Searches returned SEO pages announcing an 8th edition; no official source announces one. APA 7 remains current.

asa.notes: The asanet.org guide page links to the seventh edition (June 2022); an older news item on asanet.org still announces the sixth.

bluebook.notes: Compiled by the law reviews of Columbia, Harvard, Penn and Yale; includes a rule on AI (18.3).

chicago-18.display_name: The Chicago Manual of Style, 18th edition
chicago-18.notes: Published in September 2024. The 17th remains accessible on CMOS Online during the life of the 18th.

colombia-legal-hybrid.display_name: Colombian legal citation practice (not an official standard)
colombia-legal-hybrid.edition: Documented practice without an official standard: APA 7 with an adaptation of the Bluebook, or Chicago notes plus the Bluebook
colombia-legal-hybrid.notes: Based on an editorial manual and university guides; not an official standard.

cse.notes: Three systems: citation-sequence, citation-name and name-year.

harvard.edition: No single standard; main variant Cite Them Right (13th ed., 26-Jun-2025)
harvard.notes: Institutional and national variants. The URL of the publisher's product page was corrected.

icontec-colombia.notes: Unifies NTC 1486:2018 (7th update) and NTC 6166:2016. NTC 6166:2016 had annulled and replaced NTC 5613:2008 and NTC 4490:1998.

ieee.edition: IEEE Editorial Style Manual for Authors and IEEE Reference Guide (online edition 2024/2025)
ieee.notes: The official page confirms that it is current, but the exact version and date of the Reference Guide remain unspecified. The skill's CSL implements version 11.29.2023.

iso-690.notes: Verified in the catalogs of UNE and DIN Media, ISO member bodies; the iso.org page blocked automated reading. Cancels and replaces ISO 690:2010.

mla-9.notes: A third-party source consulted by the maintainers agrees: 9th current, no 10th.

oscola.edition: 5th (official PDF published online in March 2026; includes rule 3.7.13 on generative AI)
oscola.notes: Corrects the earlier claim that the 5th edition was from 2024. Keeps legacy support for the 4th (2012).

vancouver-nlm.edition: ICMJE Recommendations (January 2026) + NLM Citing Medicine (2nd ed.)
vancouver-nlm.notes: ICMJE refers to Citing Medicine for formatting details. The January 2026 update added a Section V on AI.

clinical-practice-guideline-appraisal.note: Instrument for appraising clinical practice guidelines.

narrative-review.note: SANRA is a quality scale, not a formal reporting guideline.

prediction-model.note: TRIPOD+AI (2024) replaces TRIPOD 2015; TRIPOD-LLM applies to language models.
